title: Grade 9 Science — Tissues
description: Tissues — Plant and Animal Tissues (CBSE Ch. 6) practice questions
subject: science

questions.question: A group of cells having similar structure and performing a common function is called:
questions.explanation: A tissue is a group of cells with similar structure, origin, and function. Tissues combine to form organs (e.g., heart, lungs), which combine into organ systems.

questions.question: The meristematic tissue in plants is responsible for:
questions.explanation: Meristematic tissue consists of actively dividing cells. It is found at the growing tips (apical), nodes (intercalary), and sides (lateral) of plants, and is responsible for plant growth.

questions.question: Xylem tissue in plants is responsible for:
questions.explanation: Xylem is a complex permanent tissue that transports water and dissolved minerals upward from roots to leaves. Phloem transports food (sugar) from leaves to other parts.

questions.question: Chlorenchyma is a type of parenchyma that:
questions.explanation: Chlorenchyma is parenchyma containing chloroplasts. It is found in leaves (mesophyll) and performs photosynthesis. Regular parenchyma stores food; collenchyma provides flexible support; sclerenchyma gives rigid support.

questions.question: Sclerenchyma tissue has cells with:
questions.explanation: Sclerenchyma cells are dead at maturity and have thick, lignified (wood-like) walls. They provide rigidity and mechanical strength to plant organs such as stems, seed coats, and the shell of a coconut.

questions.question: The tissue that forms the outer protective layer of a leaf is called:
questions.explanation: The epidermis is the outermost protective layer of plants. In leaves, it is usually one cell thick, has no chloroplasts (except guard cells), and secretes a waxy cuticle to reduce water loss.

questions.question: The basic tissue type found in animals that covers body surfaces and lines organs is:
questions.explanation: Epithelial tissue forms the lining of body surfaces, organs, and cavities (e.g., skin, gut lining, lung lining). It protects, absorbs, and secretes.

questions.question: Cartilage is a type of:
questions.explanation: Cartilage is specialised connective tissue with a matrix of chondrin. It provides flexibility and support (e.g., in the ear pinna, nose tip, between vertebrae). Bone, blood, and fat are also connective tissues.

questions.question: Striated (voluntary) muscles are found in:
questions.explanation: Striated (skeletal/voluntary) muscles are attached to bones and control body movements. They show cross-striations under a microscope. Cardiac muscle (heart) is also striated but involuntary; smooth muscles line internal organs.

questions.question: The neuron is the structural and functional unit of:
questions.explanation: A neuron (nerve cell) is the basic unit of nervous tissue. It consists of a cell body (cyton), dendrites (receivers), and an axon (transmitter). Neurons transmit electrical impulses.

questions.question: Which of the following is a fluid connective tissue?
questions.explanation: Blood is a fluid connective tissue — it has a liquid matrix (plasma) containing red blood cells, white blood cells, and platelets. Lymph is another fluid connective tissue.

questions.question: Cork (bark) cells are dead and filled with a substance called:
questions.explanation: Cork cells are dead and their walls are impregnated with suberin, a waxy substance that makes them impermeable to water and gases. Cork is the outermost layer of the bark in older stems.

questions.question: Aerenchyma is parenchyma with large air spaces. It is found in:
questions.explanation: Aerenchyma has large intercellular air spaces that help aquatic plants (hydrophytes) float and enable gas exchange in submerged tissues. Examples: water lily, lotus.

questions.question: The type of epithelium lining the respiratory tract (trachea) that sweeps out dust is:
questions.explanation: Ciliated columnar epithelium lines the trachea and bronchi. The cilia beat to sweep mucus and trapped dust particles upward and out of the respiratory tract, protecting the lungs.

questions.question: Tendons connect muscles to bones. They are made of:
questions.explanation: Tendons are made of dense regular connective tissue — tightly packed parallel collagen fibres that give great tensile strength. Ligaments (bone-to-bone) are similar but have some elastic fibres.
